sketches.mechanism: The `finally` block always executes, even after a return statement — the goodbye happens regardless of outcome.
sketches.resonance: No matter how the story ends, some things must still be said.

sketches.mechanism: In Lua, weak tables allow the garbage collector to reclaim entries even while they are still keyed — references do not prevent forgetting.
sketches.resonance: Holding someone in a weak table means you remember them only as long as the world does; the moment everyone else lets go, so do you.
sketches.draft:
memory = setmetatable({}, {__mode = "v"})

function meet(soul)
  memory[soul] = soul
end

meet({})
meet({})

collectgarbage()

-- memory is empty

sketches.mechanism: Ruby's `method_missing` is invoked when calling a method that doesn't exist — the object responds to every name, but has nothing real to give.
sketches.resonance: The loneliest thing is something that answers every call but has never truly been asked.
sketches.draft:
class Loneliness
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    self
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(*, **)
    true
  end
end

Loneliness.new.are_you_there?.do_you_hear_me?.please
